timeline.title: Enactment of the Principal Act
timeline.description: The original Goa Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 is passed by the Goa Legislative Assembly, receiving the Governor's assent on July 9, 1994. It establishes a two-tier rural local self-governance system consisting of Village Panchayats and Zilla Panchayats in conformity with the 73rd Constitutional Amendment.
keyChanges: Established the baseline structure of Village Panchayats, Taluka reference units, and Zilla Panchayats.
Set up Gram Sabha membership representing all electors in a village (Section 4).
Created initial frameworks for building permissions under Section 66 and licensing under Section 47.

timeline.title: First Amendment Act, 1996
timeline.description: Brings in major changes to the executive powers of the Panchayat, the election of office bearers, and the appeal processes for building permissions.
keyChanges: Substituted Section 47 to grant specific executive licensing, stop-work, and execution powers to the Panchayat Secretary.
Substituted Section 66(2) to define the 30-day appeal process to the Deputy Director for building permissions.
Inserted a co-opted member proviso under Section 7(4) for Scheduled Castes where reservation was not viable.

timeline.title: State Election Commissioner Rules, 1997
timeline.description: Establishes terms of service and administrative powers for the autonomous State Election Commissioner of Goa.
keyChanges: Defined tenure, salary structure, and allowances of the Commissioner.
Strengthened independent supervision over local panchayat and municipality elections.

timeline.title: Second Amendment Act, 1999
timeline.description: A landmark amendment that completely overhauls the local governance framework by introducing Taluka Panchayats, expanding Zilla Panchayat structures, and strengthening Gram Sabha participation.
keyChanges: Substituted Sections 5 and 6, expanding Gram Sabha ordinary meetings to four times a year and detailing a comprehensive list of functions and committees.
Inserted Chapters IV-A to IV-G constituting the Taluka Panchayats.
Incorporated Taluka Panchayats into the State Finance Commission's review scope.

timeline.title: Third Amendment Act, 2000
timeline.description: Deemed to have come into force from December 15, 1999, this update focuses on elections and disqualification criteria.
keyChanges: Refined conditions under which members could face disqualification under Section 10.
Aligned representation parameters for reserved seats.

timeline.title: Amendment Act, 2001
timeline.description: Deemed to have come into force from December 6, 2000, this update streamlines building repair permission procedures for villagers.
keyChanges: Amended Section 66 to permit the alteration of tiles to R.C.C. slab roofing for pre-existing single dwelling units without full development permission, subject to structural stability certification.

timeline.title: Amendment Act, 2001 (May)
timeline.description: Brings minor administrative modifications to reservation policies and financial controls.
keyChanges: Refined reservation criteria for women and backward classes in the local body elections.

timeline.title: Amendment Act, 2002 (Jan)
timeline.description: Updates financial audit mandates and administrative timelines for Panchayat funds.
keyChanges: Strengthened inspection procedures and audit regulations for local body accounts.

timeline.title: Sixth Amendment Act, 2002
timeline.description: Deemed to have come into force from April 1, 2002, this amendment focuses on financial allocations and budgeting.
keyChanges: Modified administrative procedures for preparing budgets and raising municipal funds.

timeline.title: Seventh Amendment Act, 2003
timeline.description: Introduces anti-defection and vacancy provisions for elected panchayat members who also contest or hold assembly/parliamentary seats.
keyChanges: Inserted Section 10A to declare a Panchayat member's seat vacant if they are elected to Parliament or the State Legislative Assembly.

timeline.title: Eighth Amendment Act, 2003
timeline.description: Deemed to have come into force from April 1, 2003, this update streamlines general revenue sharing and taxation procedures.
keyChanges: Refined tax collection rules and house tax calculations under Chapter VII.

timeline.title: Amendment Act, 2007
timeline.description: Deemed to have come into force from December 4, 2006, this amendment updates election rules and office-bearer disqualifications.
keyChanges: Further detailed disqualification query procedures under Section 12.

timeline.title: Amendment Act, 2010
timeline.description: Brings audit mandates, budget requirements, and structural controls into line with modern state guidelines.
keyChanges: Implemented strict financial audit regulations and penalties for non-compliance.

timeline.title: Amendment Act, 2015
timeline.description: Focuses on decentralization and local public planning groups.
keyChanges: Inserted Section 65 to mandate the establishment of Ward Development Committees for local micro-planning.

timeline.title: Amendment Act, 2021
timeline.description: Empowers state authorities to call public interest meetings and refines structural clearance criteria for residential properties.
keyChanges: Amended Section 5 to allow the Director of Panchayats to mandate extraordinary Gram Sabha meetings in public interest.
Refined the building code exception under Section 66 to exempt minor maintenance (painting, plastering, flooring) from licensing.

timeline.title: Amendment Act, 2023
timeline.description: Introduces strict enforcement powers to seal unauthorized commercial premises and streamlines trade licensing to promote ease of doing business.
keyChanges: Amended Section 47 to authorize the Block Development Officer to issue trade licenses if the Secretary fails to act within 30 days.
Inserted Section 72-A, giving the Secretary power to seal premises operating unlicensed businesses.

timeline.title: Amendment Act, 2025
timeline.description: A landmark amendment targeting administrative delays by cutting building permission review periods in half and introducing a deemed approval clause.
keyChanges: Substituted Section 66(2) to reduce building permission processing times from 30 days to 15 days.
Introduced the 'Deemed Permission' clause, allowing applicants to proceed with construction if the Panchayat fails to respond within 15 days, provided technical clearances are met.
